newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends down on Central Bank cue.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends down on Central Bank cue.

text.p: *Market jittery after Central Bank adjusts offer rate
The Philippine peso closed weaker in a jittery market on Wednesday after the Central Bank raised its offer rate for the dollar to 26.29 from 26.28 in the last thirty minutes of trading, traders said.
It settled last at its day-low of 26.288 from 26.266.
"People got scared. People covered their short positions," said a foreign bank dealer, after the Central Bank moved away its offer rate for the dollar.
"If the Central Bank's trying to send a signal it's (the peso) not going to stable, then a lot of dollars could go out," said the same dealer.

Some dealers think arbitrage money was leaving after the Central Bank lowered its term reverse repo rates. Its one-month bill had a rate of 11.125 from a previous 11.25 percent; its two months had 11.25 from 11.375; and the three months had 11.5 from 11.375.
But the first trader said the adjustment in rates was not so much as to trigger banks to cover their short dollar positions.
